text:
Predicates:
SpillsFood(x) ::: x spills a lot of food on their clothing.
NotablyTidy(x) ::: x is notably tidy.
ClumsyFoodie(x) ::: x is a clumsy foodie.
GoesOutFrequent(x) ::: x goes out frequently to find new food restaurants.
Cleanly(x) ::: x is cleanly.
ValuesOrderAndSpotlessness(x) ::: x values order and spotlessness.
PrioritizesOrderAndSpotlessness(x) ::: x's family prioritizes order and spotlessness.
Peter ::: a specific individual named Peter.

Premises:
∀x (SpillsFood(x) → ¬NotablyTidy(x)) ::: If people spill food, then they are not notably tidy.
∀x (ClumsyFoodie(x) ∧ GoesOutFrequent(x) → SpillsFood(x)) ::: Clumsy foodies who go out frequently spill food.
∀x (Cleanly(x) → NotablyTidy(x)) ::: Clean people are notably tidy.
∀x (ValuesOrderAndSpotlessness(x) → Cleanly(x)) ::: Valuing order and spotlessness implies being cleanly.
∀x (PrioritizesOrderAndSpotlessness(x) → ValuesOrderAndSpotlessness(x)) ::: Families prioritizing order and spotlessness lead individuals to value order and spotlessness.
PeterIsClumsyAndClean ::: Peter is a person who spills food and is cleanly.
PeterIsNotClumsyAndNotCleanly ::: Alternatively, Peter is not clumsy and not cleanly.

Conclusion:
PeterIsNotablyTidy ::: Whether Peter is notably tidy.
